notes: LG Greece lists the S95TR at 9.1.5 with rear speakers included; LG Canada's page and the US listings describe the same four-piece set - nine ear-level channels, five up-firing channels, a wireless subwoofer and two wireless rears. More height channels than anything else here (the centre-up channel is the fifth). The rears carry sound wirelessly but still need a mains socket. Reviewers rate its height effects below Samsung's and Sonos', which the review score reflects.

LG Greece prints 5.1.3 with rear speakers included: three height channels (two up-firing plus the centre-up channel), a wireless subwoofer and wireless rears in the box. The Cypriot listings call it 'Home Theater Soundbar with Dolby Atmos 5.1.3 Channels', which agrees.

Printed as 3.1.3 by both Electroline and Stephanis: up-firing and side-firing drivers plus a wireless subwoofer, designed to sit under an LG C-series TV on its own matching stand. Three height channels in a bar this small is unusual; the layout follows the retailer listings, not an LG spec page, so confirm before buying.

11.1.4 with six up-firing drivers, a wireless subwoofer with two 8-inch drivers, and rear speakers that detach from the ends of the bar, charge in place and then run on battery - the only system here whose rears need no mains socket. JBL's own page quotes 2470 W peak; Notebookcheck quotes 2370 W, so treat the power figure as marketing either way.
7.1.4 with up-firing drivers, detachable battery-powered wireless rears and a 10-inch wireless subwoofer. The step below the 1300MK2: same trick, fewer ear-level channels.

The MK1 of the detachable-rears flagship, printed as 11.1.4 by Stephanis and still stocked alongside the MK2. Watched so the bot can tell you when the old one is cleared out cheaply; specs follow the retailer listing and JBL's MK1 marketing rather than a current spec page.
MK1, printed as 7.1.4 with detachable wireless rears and a 10-inch wireless subwoofer. Same caveat as the Bar 1300: retailer listing, not a current spec page.

5.1.2 with detachable wireless rears and a wireless subwoofer, printed that way by Electroline. Note the trap in this family: the newer Bar 800MK2 dropped the up-firing drivers and is on the rejected list, so the MK1 and the MK2 are not interchangeable despite the names.
